title: Novel Identified complement regulatory functions of physiological proteins: Mechanisms, physiological relevance and potential for therapeutic applications
summary: The research project will investigate whether the body's own proteins have a regulatory function on a special part of the defense system, the so-called complement system. An overactivated complement system leads, among other things, to kidney diseases, which can lead to permanent damage to the kidneys or even to a complete loss of function. These include, for example, atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome and C3 glomerulopathy. In addition, the complement system may be involved in other diseases. These include, for example, typical hemolytic uremic syndrome, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, and ANCA vasculitis, IgA nephritis, or purpura Schoenlein Hennoch nephritis. An overactivated complement system can often be detected in the blood of these patients. In this research project, blood samples from these patients will be used to investigate whether overactivation of the complement system can be influenced by the addition of physiological proteins in vitro. The findings of this research project should help to better understand the above-mentioned diseases and, if necessary, to better treat them therapeutically in the future.

interventions.name: By adding the protein of interest to serum from patients, it will be shown that the overactivated complement system can be regulated.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with the following diagnoses: typical, atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, C3 gloerulopathy, IgA nephritis, Schoenlein-Hennoch purpura nephritis or ANCA vasculitis and healthy controls.
Exclusion criteria:
missing consent to biomaterial database
